front: Le livre dont je t'ai parlé est sorti en poche.
pronunciation: [luh LEE-vruh dohn zhuh tay par-LAY eh sor-tee ahn POSH]
back: The book I told you about is out in paperback.
context: 'Dont' replaces 'de + noun': parler DE ce livre → le livre DONT je t'ai parlé.

front: C'est une amie dont je suis très fière.
pronunciation: [seh tün nah-mee dohn zhuh swee treh FYEHR]
back: She's a friend I'm very proud of.
context: 'Être fier de' → dont.

front: La maison dont les volets sont bleus appartient à ma tante.
pronunciation: [lah meh-zohn dohn lay voh-leh sohn BLUH ah-par-tyan ah mah TAHNT]
back: The house whose shutters are blue belongs to my aunt.
context: 'Dont' also means 'whose'. Word order: dont + subject + verb.

front: Ce dont j'ai besoin, c'est d'un peu de calme.
pronunciation: [suh dohn zhay buh-ZWAN, seh dan puh duh KALM]
back: What I need is a bit of peace and quiet.
context: 'Ce dont' = what (with de-verbs: avoir besoin de, parler de).

front: Ce que je préfère, c'est le silence du matin.
pronunciation: [suh kuh zhuh pray-FEHR, seh luh see-lahns dü mah-TAN]
back: What I like best is the morning silence.
context: 'Ce que' = what (direct object).

front: Ce qui m'inquiète, c'est son silence.
pronunciation: [suh kee man-KYET, seh sohn see-LAHNS]
back: What worries me is his silence.
context: 'Ce qui' = what (subject).

front: L'entreprise pour laquelle je travaille est très connue.
pronunciation: [lahn-truh-preez poor lah-kel zhuh trah-vahy eh treh koh-NÜ]
back: The company I work for is very well known.
context: After a preposition, use lequel/laquelle/lesquels/lesquelles for things.

front: Le stylo avec lequel j'écris ne marche plus bien.
pronunciation: [luh stee-loh ah-vek luh-kel zhay-kree nuh marsh plü BYAN]
back: The pen I'm writing with doesn't work well anymore.
context: 'Avec lequel' = with which.

front: Les raisons pour lesquelles il est parti restent floues.
pronunciation: [lay reh-zohn poor lay-kel ee leh par-TEE rest FLOO]
back: The reasons why he left remain unclear.
context: 'Lesquelles' agrees with 'raisons' (feminine plural).

front: Le projet auquel je pense est ambitieux.
pronunciation: [luh proh-zheh oh-kel zhuh pahns eh tahn-bee-SYUH]
back: The project I'm thinking of is ambitious.
context: À + lequel = auquel; à + lesquels = auxquels; à + laquelle = à laquelle.

front: Les clients auxquels nous avons écrit n'ont pas répondu.
pronunciation: [lay klee-yahn oh-kel noo zah-vohn zay-KREE nohn pah ray-pohn-DÜ]
back: The clients we wrote to haven't replied.
context: 'Écrire à' → auxquels.

front: Le parc près duquel nous habitons est magnifique.
pronunciation: [luh park preh dü-KEL noo zah-bee-tohn eh mah-nyee-FEEK]
back: The park near which we live is magnificent.
context: De + lequel = duquel (with compound prepositions: près de, à côté de, au bout de).

front: La personne à qui j'ai parlé était très aimable.
pronunciation: [lah pehr-sun ah kee zhay par-lay ay-teh treh zeh-MAH-bluh]
back: The person I spoke to was very kind.
context: For people after a preposition, 'qui' is preferred: à qui, avec qui.

front: La ville où je suis né a beaucoup changé.
pronunciation: [lah veel oo zhuh swee nay ah boh-koo shahn-ZHAY]
back: The city where I was born has changed a lot.
context: 'Où' = where (place).

front: Le jour où on s'est rencontrés, il pleuvait.
pronunciation: [luh zhoor oo ohn seh rahn-kohn-TRAY, eel pluh-VEH]
back: The day we met, it was raining.
context: 'Où' is also used for time in French: le jour où, l'année où (never 'le jour que').

front: Le pont a été construit au XIXe siècle.
pronunciation: [luh pohn ah ay-tay kohns-trwee oh deez-nuh-vyem SYEH-kluh]
back: The bridge was built in the 19th century.
context: Passive: être + participle agreeing with the subject.

front: Les résultats seront annoncés demain.
pronunciation: [lay ray-zül-TAH suh-rohn tah-nohn-SAY duh-MAN]
back: The results will be announced tomorrow.
context: Future passive.

front: Ce tableau a été peint par Monet.
pronunciation: [suh tah-bloh ah ay-tay pan par moh-NEH]
back: This painting was painted by Monet.
context: 'Par' introduces the agent.

front: Le directeur est respecté de tous.
pronunciation: [luh dee-rek-tuhr eh res-pek-tay duh TOOS]
back: The director is respected by everyone.
context: With feelings and states, 'de' can introduce the agent: aimé de, respecté de.

front: On a volé ma voiture.
pronunciation: [ohn nah voh-lay mah vwah-TÜR]
back: My car was stolen.
context: French often prefers 'on' + active over the passive.

front: Ça se mange froid.
pronunciation: [sah suh mahnzh FRWAH]
back: It's eaten cold.
context: Passive meaning with 'se': ça se dit, ça se fait, ça se vend bien.

front: Il s'est fait voler son portefeuille.
pronunciation: [eel seh feh voh-lay sohn port-FUHY]
back: He had his wallet stolen.
context: 'Se faire' + infinitive = to have something done to you.

front: Je me suis fait couper les cheveux.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh swee feh koo-pay lay shuh-VUH]
back: I had my hair cut.
context: 'Se faire' + infinitive for services you get done.

front: C'est moi qui ai appelé le médecin.
pronunciation: [seh MWAH kee ay ah-puh-lay luh mayd-SAN]
back: I'm the one who called the doctor.
context: Emphasis: c'est… qui. The verb agrees with the pronoun: c'est moi qui AI.

front: C'est à Lyon que je l'ai rencontré.
pronunciation: [seh tah lee-OHN kuh zhuh lay rahn-kohn-TRAY]
back: It was in Lyon that I met him.
context: Emphasis on a complement: c'est… que.

front: Ce sont mes parents qui m'ont appris à lire.
pronunciation: [suh sohn may pah-rahn kee mohn tah-pree ah LEER]
back: It was my parents who taught me to read.
context: 'Ce sont' + plural.

front: Moi, le café, je le prends sans sucre.
pronunciation: [MWAH, luh kah-FAY, zhuh luh prahn sahn SÜ-kruh]
back: Me, I take my coffee without sugar.
context: Dislocation: topic first, then a pronoun. Extremely common in spoken French.

front: Il est arrivé, ton colis ?
pronunciation: [ee leh tah-ree-VAY, tohn koh-LEE]
back: Has your parcel arrived?
context: Right dislocation: subject repeated at the end. Typical spoken French.

front: Ce que j'aime chez lui, c'est son humour.
pronunciation: [suh kuh zhem shay LWEE, seh sohn nü-MOOR]
back: What I like about him is his sense of humor.
context: 'Chez' + person = in someone's character.

front: Voilà pourquoi je suis en retard.
pronunciation: [vwah-lah poor-KWAH zhuh swee zahn ruh-TAR]
back: That's why I'm late.
context: 'Voilà pourquoi' = that's why.

front: Non seulement il est en retard, mais en plus il n'a pas ses documents.
pronunciation: [nohn suhl-MAHN ee leh tahn ruh-TAR, meh ahn PLÜS eel nah pah say doh-kü-MAHN]
back: Not only is he late, but on top of that he doesn't have his documents.
context: 'Non seulement… mais (en plus)' = not only… but also.

front: Plus on attend, plus c'est cher.
pronunciation: [plü zohn nah-TAHN, plü seh SHEHR]
back: The longer you wait, the more expensive it gets.
context: Parallel structure.

front: Tout ce que tu dis est vrai.
pronunciation: [too suh kuh tü dee eh VREH]
back: Everything you say is true.
context: 'Tout ce que' = everything (that).

front: Quel que soit le prix, je l'achète.
pronunciation: [kel kuh swah luh PREE, zhuh lah-SHET]
back: Whatever the price, I'm buying it.
context: 'Quel(le)(s) que soit' + noun = whatever; quel agrees with the noun.

front: Où que tu ailles, je te suivrai.
pronunciation: [oo kuh tü AHY, zhuh tuh swee-VREH]
back: Wherever you go, I'll follow you.
context: 'Où que' + subjunctive = wherever.

front: Si fatigué qu'il soit, il ne se plaint jamais.
pronunciation: [see fah-tee-gay keel SWAH, eel nuh suh plan zhah-MEH]
back: However tired he may be, he never complains.
context: 'Si + adjective + que' + subjunctive = however… (also 'aussi… que').

front: N'ayant pas reçu de réponse, je vous relance.
pronunciation: [neh-yahn pah ruh-sü duh ray-POHNS, zhuh voo ruh-LAHNS]
back: Not having received a reply, I'm following up.
context: Present participle (ayant) in formal writing, expressing cause.

front: Étant donné la situation, nous reportons la réunion.
pronunciation: [ay-tahn doh-nay lah see-tü-ah-SYOHN, noo ruh-por-tohn lah ray-ü-NYOHN]
back: Given the situation, we're postponing the meeting.
context: 'Étant donné' = given (invariable before the noun).

front: Le contrat signé, les travaux ont commencé.
pronunciation: [luh kohn-trah see-NYAY, lay trah-voh ohn koh-mahn-SAY]
back: Once the contract was signed, work began.
context: Absolute participle construction: formal and concise.

front: Il parle comme s'il savait tout.
pronunciation: [eel parl kum seel sah-veh TOO]
back: He talks as if he knew everything.
context: 'Comme si' + imparfait = as if.

front: Il travaille d'autant plus qu'il veut être promu.
pronunciation: [eel trah-vahy doh-tahn plüs keel vuh eh-truh proh-MÜ]
back: He works all the more because he wants to be promoted.
context: 'D'autant plus que' = all the more because.

front: Il a beau essayer, il n'y arrive pas.
pronunciation: [ee lah boh eh-seh-YAY, eel nee ah-reev PAH]
back: No matter how hard he tries, he can't do it.
context: 'Avoir beau' + infinitive = however much, in vain.

front: À peine était-il arrivé qu'il est reparti.
pronunciation: [ah pen ay-teh-teel ah-ree-VAY keel eh ruh-par-TEE]
back: No sooner had he arrived than he left again.
context: 'À peine' at the start of a sentence triggers inversion (formal).

front: Peut-être viendra-t-il demain.
pronunciation: [puh-teh-truh vyan-drah-TEEL duh-MAN]
back: Perhaps he'll come tomorrow.
context: Formal: 'peut-être' at the start → inversion. In speech: 'peut-être qu'il viendra'.

front: Reste à savoir qui va payer.
pronunciation: [rest ah sah-VWAHR kee vah peh-YAY]
back: It remains to be seen who will pay.
context: 'Reste à' + infinitive (impersonal) = it remains to.
